data.title: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity
data.summary: An Oregon man is now in federal custody and charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity after he allegedly met a Utah minor online in May 2025, drove to Utah to pick up the victim, and then transported the victim to his residence across state lines.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/utah-mino.label: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity

data.title: Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme
data.summary: A federal grand jury in the Central District of California returned an indictment yesterday charging Marisela Nuno, 53, of Los Angeles, California, with an $18 million scheme to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program, federal stimulus programs authorized as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/los-angel.label: Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme

data.title: Oklahoma Man Charged in Connection with Sending Threatening Letters Containing Non-Toxic White Powder to Election and Government Officials Across the Country
data.summary: Robin Patrick Martin, 67, of Oklahoma City, has been charged with conveying false or misleading information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications in connection with threatening letters mailed to state election officials, members of Congress, the FBI and others.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/oklahoma-.label: Oklahoma Man Charged in Connection with Sending Threatening Letters Containing Non-Toxic White Powder to Election and Government Officials Across the Country

data.title: Former U.S. Government Contractor Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia
data.summary: Abraham Teklu Lemma, 53, of Maryland, a former information technology contractor at the National Reconnaissance Office, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Department of Justice pleaded guilty today to conspiring to commit espionage on behalf of the government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/former-us.label: Former U.S. Government Contractor Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia

data.title: Defense and Aerospace Contractors ILC Dover and ILC Astrospace Agree to Pay $13M to Resolve Cybersecurity Fraud Allegations
data.summary: Defense and aerospace companies ILC Dover LP and ILC Astrospace LLC, of Frederica, Delaware, have agreed to pay $13 million to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by failing to comply with cybersecurity requirements in their contracts with the Department of the Army, the Missile Defense Agency, and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/defense-a.label: Defense and Aerospace Contractors ILC Dover and ILC Astrospace Agree to Pay $13M to Resolve Cybersecurity Fraud Allegations

data.title: Ohio Pet Breeder Agrees to Surrender Over 1,100 Chinchillas
data.summary: The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio endorsed a consent decree entered between the United States and the owner of R & R Chinchilla Inc. to surrender over 300 remaining chinchillas at a breeding facility in Jenera, Ohio. The court order follows R & R Chinchilla’s voluntary surrender of roughly 800 additional chinchillas to animal welfare organizations pursuant to a modified temporary restraining order.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/ohio-pet-.label: Ohio Pet Breeder Agrees to Surrender Over 1,100 Chinchillas

data.summary: Yesterday, the Justice Department awarded East Baton Rouge Parish $63,532,285 million through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in communities across the country.

data.title: Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads to Mexican Federal Judge’s Arrest on U.S. Charges of Accepting $2 Million Bribe to Free Canadian Drug Trafficker Charged with Ryan Wedding
data.summary: A Mexican judge has been arrested on a nine-count federal indictment charging him with accepting a $2 million bribe in exchange for granting bond to and ordering the release of a Canadian drug trafficker who was the second-in-command to a former Olympic snowboarder charged with leading a transnational cocaine trafficking operation and with murder and attempted murder, the Justice Department announced today.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/homeland-.label: Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads to Mexican Federal Judge’s Arrest on U.S. Charges of Accepting $2 Million Bribe to Free Canadian Drug Trafficker Charged with Ryan Wedding

data.title: The Department of Justice Files Complaint Against the Pennsylvania State University Challenging Its Policy that Provide In-State Tuition to Illegal Aliens
data.summary: Today, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against the Pennsylvania State University for violating federal law by prioritizing the needs of illegal aliens over U.S. citizens in defiance of Congress’s commands. The Department is challenging the Pennsylvania State University’s policy which grants in-state tuition to illegal aliens while denying reduced tuition to U.S. citizens. This policy unconstitutionally discriminates against U.S. citizens who are not afforded the same reduced tuition rate, in direct conflict with federal law.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/departmen.label: The Department of Justice Files Complaint Against the Pennsylvania State University Challenging Its Policy that Provide In-State Tuition to Illegal Aliens

data.title: U.S. Trustee Program Prevails at Trial to Revoke $3.9M Discharge from Seattle Man Who Concealed Inheritance Rights and Business Interest
data.summary: A Seattle man who concealed an inheritance and his interest in a business lost his bankruptcy discharge of more than $3.9 million after a trial victory by the Justice Department’s U.S. Trustee Program (USTP).

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/us-truste.label: U.S. Trustee Program Prevails at Trial to Revoke $3.9M Discharge from Seattle Man Who Concealed Inheritance Rights and Business Interest

data.title: Department of Justice Launches Super Intelligence Task Force
data.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice is announcing the formation of its Super Intelligence (SI) Task Force (DOJ-SITF). President Trump has made clear that “America stands at the forefront of a new technological revolution in intelligence,” and the Department will be a leader in safeguarding against malicious SI actors.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/departmen.label: Department of Justice Launches Super Intelligence Task Force

data.title: Texas Man Indicted for Sex Trafficking and Obstruction Offenses
data.summary: A federal grand jury in the Northern District of Texas returned an eight-count superseding indictment charging Felix Omoruyi, 39, of DeSoto, Texas, with sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion, sex trafficking of a minor, and related charges.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/texas-man.label: Texas Man Indicted for Sex Trafficking and Obstruction Offenses

data.title: Cleveland Gang Members Convicted of Racketeering, Murder, Kidnapping, Drug Trafficking, and Firearms Offenses
data.summary: Following a three-week trial, a federal jury in Cleveland convicted three members of the Fully Blooded Felons, a violent Cleveland street gang, of a number of crimes, including Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) Act murder, RICO conspiracy, RICO kidnapping, drug trafficking, and gun crimes.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/cleveland.label: Cleveland Gang Members Convicted of Racketeering, Murder, Kidnapping, Drug Trafficking, and Firearms Offenses

data.title: CEO and VA Employee Sentenced for Paying and Receiving Illegal Health Care Kickbacks and Bribes
data.summary: Two Florida men were sentenced today for their roles in a conspiracy to pay and receive illegal health care kickbacks. Laurent Cassagnol was sentenced to 6 months in prison, and Heriberto Rivera was sentenced to 13 months in prison. In addition to the prison terms, Cassagnol was ordered to forfeit $175,172, and Rivera was ordered to forfeit $515,542, which represented the proceeds that the defendants obtained from the offense.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/ceo-and-v.label: CEO and VA Employee Sentenced for Paying and Receiving Illegal Health Care Kickbacks and Bribes

data.title: Justice Department Says Federal Education Aid Cannot Be Tied to Unconstitutional Race-Based Criteria
data.summary: Today, the Department of Justice’s Office of Legal Counsel issued an opinion clarifying the limits on the Department of Education’s authority to consider race when administering the Magnet Schools Assistance Program (MSAP). MSAP is a federal grant program designed to promote voluntary school desegregation and expand educational opportunities for students through competitive grants to school districts. The opinion reaffirms the federal government’s longstanding support for magnet schools while ensuring that federal assistance is not conditioned on unconstitutional race‑based criteria.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Says Federal Education Aid Cannot Be Tied to Unconstitutional Race-Based Criteria

data.title: Reward Offers Up to $50M for Information Leading to Arrests and/or Convictions of Foreign Terrorist Organization Tren de Aragua (TdA) Leaders Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
data.summary: Note : Read the Superseding Indictment here. Foreign Terrorist Organization Tren de Aragua (TdA) leaders Yohan José Romero, also known as “Yohan Petrica,” 48; Giovanni Vicente Mosquera Serrano, also known as “El Viejo,” 37; and Juan Gabriel Rivas Núñez, also known as “Juancho,” 44, were previously charged in a 2025 six-count second superseding indictment in the Southern District of Texas, for conspiring to provide and providing material support to TdA. A nine-count third superseding indictment was later returned in July 2026 and unsealed this week. In those indictments, Mosquera Serrano is also charged with conspiracy to manufacture and distribute cocaine and international cocaine distribution.

data.title: 14 Charged in Deadly Human Smuggling Scheme That Killed 7 Aliens Earlier This Year
data.summary: A federal grand jury in the Western District of Texas returned a superseding indictment charging a total of 14 individuals, including seven illegal aliens, three non-citizens, and four U.S. citizens, for their roles in a conspiracy to smuggle aliens into the United States for profit. This included a failed human smuggling event that resulted in the deaths of seven people, including one child, who died after being loaded into a poorly ventilated shipping container.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/14-charge.label: 14 Charged in Deadly Human Smuggling Scheme That Killed 7 Aliens Earlier This Year
